doc.route.post.api.schedules.text: Create a job schedule: `kind` (a registered job kind) plus a cadence. `interval` wants `interval_seconds` (at least 60); `daily` and `weekly` want `at_minute` (the whole minute of the local day, 0 to 1439) and a `timezone`, which defaults to the caller's own; `weekly` also wants `days_of_week`, a comma-separated set of 0-6 with Sunday as 0. Optionally `payload`, `requirements`, `priority`, `name` and `paused`. The first firing is never immediate. The timezone is stored ON the schedule rather than resolved from its owner when it fires: a schedule is a standing instruction, and if its author travels and changes their profile, "07:00 before the morning meeting" must not silently move for everybody else. The schedule runs as the CALLER, whose authority every job it fires then spends — an unknown kind is refused here rather than enqueueing work nothing can run, for ever.

doc.tool.doc_set_type.text: Record the document type a PERSON decided, after a review. The label is held to the same label set the classification offered, so a type no trigger could match is refused rather than stored. An EMPTY label withdraws the type — the honest record of a rejection, since there is no doc_type of "unknown". Writes doc_type / doc_type_confidence / doc_type_source with source "review" and confidence 1.00, and versions <key>.classification.json beside the document so the backend's original guess stays in its history.

doc.route.post.api.workers.jobs.id.deriv.text: Write a document DERIVED from one THIS job names (issue #62): {source, key, bytes_b64, claim_token, content_type?, filename?}. The write counterpart of the read above, under the same three conditions — the caller holds this attempt, `source` appears in the job's own payload, and the write happens as the job's user, so files:write, the storage quotas and the org gate all apply. The output takes the source's visibility and then its grants, is marked derived so an opted-in trigger cannot fire on a worker's own output, and is capped at TELEMACHUS_MAX_UPLOAD: a worker is not a way past the front door's ceiling. There is deliberately no standalone put — an output anchored to nothing would make the worker token a key to the team's repository.

That last figure is the one a deep queue cannot otherwise explain: a stalled fleet and a busy one look the same from a count. Every number is derived, and a job held by a quota is NOT counted unclaimable — GET /api/jobs already says `waiting` for that.

doc.route.post.api.login.text: Sign in with username and password (and a TOTP code when 2FA is enabled). Returns a bearer token. Attempts are throttled per address and per account with a growing delay (429 and `Retry-After`), every attempt is audited as `user.login`, and an account may be locked outright when the operator sets TELEMACHUS_LOGIN_LOCK_FAILURES (423, cleared by an operator password reset).

The new token is in this response and never again; the one it replaces keeps working for `overlap_seconds`, so the host can be redeployed without a window in which it is dead. For a worker that cannot rotate itself, and for a token believed leaked — unlike the worker's own call this one is never refused for rotating too often.

doc.route.delete.api.jobs.id.content.text: Purge a settled job's payload and result, keeping the row. Your own; somebody else's needs jobs:purge. For `infer.chat` and the document pipeline the payload IS the document's text and the result is the model's reply, so this is the lever a caller honouring a deletion request needs. Refused on a queued, running or canceling job — cancel it first, because its payload is the input a handler is about to read. Status, timings, attempt counts and the audit trail all survive; `purged_at` is reported on the job so an empty payload and a purged one can be told apart.

doc.route.post.api.workers.jobs.id.relea.text: Hand a job back WITHOUT spending an attempt (issue #61): {claim_token, reason?} — busy, unsupported or shutdown; anything else is recorded as `other` rather than refused, since the worker has already said it cannot run the job. It goes straight back to the queue and any other worker may take it at once, while the releasing executor is not offered it again for 30 seconds — the bound on a release loop, which the untouched attempt counter cannot provide. Past 10 releases the job fails instead, naming the hosts that let it go: work no worker will run needs a person.

doc.route.get.api.admin.anchor.export.text: Anchor receipts as JSONL, oldest first, for retention OUTSIDE this instance's trust domain. `?since_seq=` asks for only what a retainer does not yet hold, so the file appends. Verify a retained copy offline with `racket cli/telemachus-anchor.rkt verify <file> --public-key <hex>` — which needs neither this server nor its database, because an anchor is worth something precisely when the instance is the suspect.

doc.route.post.api.feeds.id.poll.text: Poll the feed NOW, synchronously, and land what it returns as repository objects under `feeds/<slug>/<external-id>.json` — the item's own payload as the body and the item's title in the version's filename, so it is searchable. Answers what happened: requests made, items seen, created, updated, unchanged, skipped, and the cursor it advanced to. An UNCHANGED item writes no new version (the dedup hash is over the bytes this instance would store, not over the source's `updated_at`), and the cursor only advances over items that actually landed, so a refused write is re-read rather than skipped. Bounded to ten requests because it runs on a request thread; the scheduled poll is the same work in a job, where the lease and cancellation apply. 400 for a kind this build can probe but not poll, for a feed whose user has left the team, and when the item fields would exceed the forty a team may define. `feed.fetches` is charged per REQUEST, not per item — the dimension protects the source's rate limit as much as this instance.

doc.route.delete.api.repo.text: Delete every object under `?prefix=`, cascading to what each one derived (#86). DRY RUN BY DEFAULT: without `confirm=1` nothing is removed and the reply is the count, the bytes and the ids that WOULD go. An empty or missing prefix is refused rather than read as "every object in the team". `?cascade=0` deletes only the listed objects and leaves their derivatives. doc.route.delete.api.repo-obj.id.text: Delete an object. Bytes are released when nothing in the ORG still references them — another version, another object, or an IN-FLIGHT upload's staged part. `?cascade=1` also deletes everything derived from it, transitively (the extracted JSON, the filled form, each translation), as ONE audited act; `?detach=1` with it keeps those objects and removes the derivation rows instead, so nothing claims to come from something that is gone. `?dry_run=1` reports what would go and changes nothing. A cascade is ALL-OR-NOTHING on permission: an object in the tree you may not delete refuses the whole operation by name, because a half-cascaded tree cannot be told apart from a finished one.

doc.route.get.beta-sdk.js.text: The browser SDK a Tier-B onboarding bundle loads (window.Telemachus.beta).

doc.route.get.api.oop.text: Connected sandboxed (out-of-process) plugins and the capabilities they may ask for.

doc.perm.notes:manage.text: Share notes one does not own.

ui.wkwindowhint.text: Finished, failed, and leases that expired on this host in the last 24 hours. An expiry means the host stopped answering while it held a job; the job went back to the queue.

doc.tool.doc_classify.step.text: The workflow step id, for provenance

doc.route.post.api.instance.resume.text: Hosted mode: resume a suspended tenant.

doc.route.post.api.logout.text: End the session this request is holding. The console's sign-out called nothing before this, so the bearer stayed valid until it expired.

doc.tool.doc_render.object.text: The source document's object id — the form is written beside it (default: beside the template)

doc.route.post.api.workers.jobs.id.heart.text: Extend the lease on a job this worker holds: {claim_token}, the token the claim returned. A missing or stale token is a 409.

doc.route.put.api.org.retention.text: Set the company's retention rules. Same vocabulary and same refusals as the team route; the effective value for a team is the shortest of instance, org and team.

ui.nosharedwithme.text: Nothing has been shared with you yet.

doc.route.get.api.branding.text: Title, tagline, logo and theme tokens. Public: the sign-in screen renders them. On a company's hostname, or for its signed-in user, the company's own (TEN-2d).

ui.caphint.text: View opens and downloads; edit also uploads new versions; manage also shares, revokes and changes visibility.

inbox.summary.text: You have {count, plural, one {# new message} other {# new messages}}.

doc.tool.translate_text.text: Translate text into a target language.

doc.tool.doc_set_type.rationale.text: Why, in the reviewer's own words — kept in the record, not in the attributes

ui.s3hint.text: Any S3 client works: aws-cli, rclone, boto3, Cyberduck. Your team is the bucket.

doc.route.post.api.orgs.ref.quota.text: Set an org-level quota; teams nest beneath it.

doc.route.delete.api.feeds.id.text: Delete a feed's configuration. Anything it already pulled is an ordinary repository document and is untouched — deleting the feed is not a retraction of its items.

doc.route.post.api.activate.text: Hosted mode: redeem an activation token and set the owner's password.

doc.route.post.api.l10n.discard.text: Remove a locale's machine drafts (never a human's work).

ui.wkretireconfirm.text: Retire {name}? Its worker token is revoked for good and any job it is holding goes back to the queue. To take it out of rotation for a while, drain it instead.

doc.route.post.api.feeds.text: Configure a feed: `slug` (the key prefix pulled items land under), `kind`, `url`, and optionally `auth` with its `secret` — `bearer`, `header` or `query`, the last because a great many real sources authenticate that way and refusing it only pushes the token into the URL, unsealed. The secret is sealed at rest and rotated by `telemachus-secrets rewrap`. `user_id` is the team member a pull acts as and defaults to the caller; somebody outside the team is refused, because a feed cannot act as them.

doc.tool.list_notes.text: List the current user's notes (title and visibility).

doc.tool.doc_list_unclassified.text: List repository documents under a key prefix that have no document type yet — the input to a classification backfill. Returns object ids, capped at a batch; run the backfill again to continue. A document that already carries doc_type is skipped, which is what makes a re-run free, and the outputs other runs derived are never listed.

doc.route.post.api.webhooks.text: Subscribe to events: `url` (http(s)) and `events` — `"*"` or a comma-separated subset of the names `GET /api/webhooks` lists. An unknown event name is refused rather than stored, because a subscription that silently never fires is worse than one that was rejected. The signing secret is in the reply and is SHOWN ONCE; rotate to replace it.

doc.perm.instance:*.text: Everything at the instance tier; the operator (superadmin).

doc.tool.doc_render.data.text: The data to fill in, e.g. the extracted fields

doc.route.put.api.i18n.text: Set the instance default locale and whether users may switch.

doc.perm.files:read.text: Open, download and search repository documents; read provenance and the knowledge graph.

doc.route.post.api.webhooks.id.ping.text: Deliver a `ping` event to this subscription NOW, synchronously, and answer with what happened. The way to check a receiver's signature verification before a real event depends on it. Refused with 409 if the subscription is inactive or does not subscribe to `ping`.

doc.route.post.api.notes.id.share.text: Share a note with a user (owner, or notes:manage). The permission granted must be a notes:* one.

ui.wktokenhint.text: Copy it now. It is not stored anywhere you can read it again; if it is lost, retire this worker and add another.

doc.route.post.api.instance.quota.text: Hosted mode: set a quota limit for the tenant's team.

doc.route.get.api.tools.text: Every registered tool with its permission, source and per-team enabled state.

doc.tool.kg_list_unextracted.text: List repository documents whose text has not been extracted into the knowledge graph yet (or is stale after an overwrite). Returns object ids, capped at a batch; run the index-knowledge workflow again to continue.

ui.wkunclaimablehint.text: Queued jobs that no live worker's declared models or kinds match. A job merely waiting for its team's AI budget is NOT counted here — the Jobs tab says so on the job itself.

doc.perm.org:read-data.text: Read team-visible notes, documents and search results across every team in the company (TEN-2h). Never private ones; never a write; never AI spend. Held by the org_reader role.

ui.wkdrainedok.text: Drained — it will take no new work

doc.plugin.doc-indexer.text: A workflow that extracts text from repository documents into the search index: find what is unindexed, fan out, extract. Re-run it any time; it only touches what changed.

doc.route.patch.api.repo-obj.id.attribut.text: Set a document's team-defined metadata: {attributes: {key: value}}. Needs files:write ON THE DOCUMENT. A key the team has not defined is refused, not stored; an empty value clears it.

ui.notprocessed.text: No workflow has processed this document yet.

doc.route.post.api.org.members.text: Add a person to a team in the caller's company, optionally with an org role (org_admin, org_owner, org_reader).

ui.wkconfighint.text: Declared in executors.json, which owns its names — this instance reads the file at boot. It cannot be drained or retired from here; edit the file and restart.

doc.route.put.api.org.session-policy.text: Set the company's session timeouts. Only tightening takes effect: a value looser than the instance's is answered with the instance's.

doc.route.post.api.runs.id.cancel.text: Cancel a run; a step already executing finishes, the next never starts.

doc.route.post.api.org.branding.logo.text: Upload the company's logo (base64) and make it the company's mark.

ui.brandthemehint.text: The palette this console wears — the same tokens the beta funnel uses. Changes preview live; Save applies them for everyone.

doc.route.post.api.ai.chat.text: One model turn. `prompt` is a string or a list of content parts; `response_format` ({type: text|json_object|json_schema}) rides to the model and the reply is refused if it does not honour it. Quota-admitted (ai.requests, ai.tokens.total), governed by the team's ai.concurrency. Routing to a named executor needs instance:manage. `simulated: true` on the response means NO model answered: TELEMACHUS_MODEL_URL is unset and the reply is a deterministic echo of the prompt. The key is absent on a real call.

doc.route.post.api.l10n.draft.text: Queue AI drafts for a locale's missing strings, in batches of 20 scheduler jobs, quota-metered.

doc.route.get.api.s3.credentials.text: The caller's S3 access keys (secrets never shown again) and the endpoint/bucket to use them with.

doc.route.get.api.beta.config.text: The published onboarding experience's public slice (fields, copy, theme) in one language.

ui.uploadhint.text: Any format. The path may contain slashes; uploading the same path again keeps the old copy as a version.

doc.route.get.api.feeds.id.text: One feed. Another team's id is a 404, not a 403.

doc.route.get.api.reviews.text: The team's review queue, newest first. ?status=pending (the default), decided, canceled or all.

doc.plugin.beta-onboarding.text: A customized beta funnel (founders program) registered via the SDK's init! hook.

doc.route.post.api.translate.text: Translate text into a target language, applying the team glossary.

doc.route.put.api.repo.key.text: Upload a raw body to a key (?filename=, ?visibility=); writing an existing key adds a version. Triggers evaluate here.

doc.route.patch.api.webhooks.id.text: Change `url`, `events`, `active` or `description`, and with `{"rotate": true}` mint a new signing secret — shown once, and the previous one immediately signs nothing. Validated as the subscription would be, so a patch cannot reach a state a create could not.

doc.perm.jobs:schedule.text: Create, retune, pause and delete JOB SCHEDULES — recurring work. A schedule enqueues an ordinary job on an interval, running as whoever created it, so it commits the team's AI and storage budget to spending on a timer with nobody present to watch it. Reading one is held to the same permission as writing it, because a schedule's payload is the input of every job it fires.

ui.wkaddhint.text: Creates the worker token this host signs in with. The token is shown once, here, and never again.

doc.route.get.api.2fa.recovery-codes.text: How many of the caller's recovery codes are still unspent. Never the codes themselves.

ui.wkunreportedhint.text: This worker has never said what it is doing. It was written against an older protocol, or it has not claimed yet — not a fault.

doc.route.patch.api.schedules.id.text: Retune a schedule: `cadence`, `interval_seconds`, `at_minute`, `days_of_week`, `timezone`, `paused`, `payload`, `priority`, `name`. The schedule is validated AS IT WOULD BE, so switching to `daily` in the same request that supplies `at_minute` is accepted and switching without one is refused — a patch cannot reach a state a create could not. Any change to WHEN recomputes the next firing, rather than firing once at the old time and only then obeying the edit. The PRINCIPAL cannot be patched: changing whose authority a timer spends is a new schedule, not an edit. Resuming a paused schedule moves its next firing forward instead of catching up on every tick it missed.
